original_question: Two metrics with negative curvature on a compact manifold must be isometric if they have the same marked length spectrum.
target_in_paper: Conjecture 5.1.1 in §5.1 (“Does the marked length spectrum determine the metric?”): two negatively curved metrics on a compact manifold are conjectured to be isometric when they have the same marked length spectrum. The definition of marked length spectrum is given immediately above the conjecture. ([aimath.org](https://aimath.org/pastworkshops/geodesicsproblems.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper’s exact target almost verbatim: the hypothesis is negative curvature, the setting is a compact manifold, the invariant is the marked length spectrum, and the conclusion is isometry. It also stays on the main conjecture itself rather than drifting to the neighboring boundary-rigidity or geodesic-flow-conjugacy problems. ([aimath.org](https://aimath.org/pastworkshops/geodesicsproblems.pdf))
missing_details: The paper is discussing Riemannian metrics, not arbitrary metric structures.
The two metrics are metrics on the same closed/compact manifold M.
“Negative curvature” should be spelled out as strictly negative sectional curvature everywhere.

The marked length spectrum should be defined explicitly: for each free homotopy class [gamma] of loops in M, L_g([gamma]) is the infimum of the g-lengths of loops in that class (equivalently, the length of the shortest closed geodesic in that class).
Equality of marked length spectra means L_{g1}([gamma]) = L_{g2}([gamma]) for every free homotopy class [gamma] of loops in M.
To make the statement stand-alone, “isometric” should be made explicit as: there exists a diffeomorphism phi : M -> M such that phi^* g2 = g1.
Since the paper states this as an open problem/conjecture, the refined version should be phrased as a question (“Is it true that ...?”), not as an established theorem.
refined_question: Let M be a compact manifold without boundary, and let g1 and g2 be Riemannian metrics on M with strictly negative sectional curvature. For each free homotopy class [gamma] of loops in M, let L_{g_i}([gamma]) be the infimum of the g_i-lengths of loops in [gamma] (equivalently, the length of the shortest closed geodesic in that class). If L_{g1}([gamma]) = L_{g2}([gamma]) for every free homotopy class [gamma], must there exist a diffeomorphism phi : M -> M such that phi^* g2 = g1?
justification: The nearest official formulation is exactly Conjecture 5.1.1 in §5.1, not a broader neighboring rigidity question. Section 5.1 first defines the marked length spectrum as a function on free homotopy classes, then states the conjecture in essentially your wording. The surrounding discussion adds two scope-setting facts that matter for faithfulness: the conjecture is already known for surfaces (indeed under non-positive curvature there), and it remains open in higher dimensions. The same paragraph also says that Hamenstadt showed equality of marked length spectra forces C^0-conjugacy of the geodesic flows, which reduces Conjecture 5.1.1 to the distinct but nearby Conjecture 5.2.1; that reduction is context, not an equivalent reformulation, so no alternate formulation should be supplied here. ([aimath.org](https://aimath.org/pastworkshops/geodesicsproblems.pdf))
